description.text: The objective is to minimize the negative penalized specific energy absorption of a star shaped crash-box. The design variables are the geometric parameters of the crash-box. The structure is clamped at the base and impacted by a 250 kg impactor from above at a velocity of 25.2 km/h. The evaluation budget is {MAX_EVAL_VALUE}.

The objective is to minimize the negative penalized specific energy absorption of a star shaped crash-box. The design variables are geometric parameters defining the cross-sectional shape and wall thickness of the crash-box. The structure is clamped at the base, and is impacted by a 250 kg impactor from above at a velocity of 25.2 km/h. The evaluation budget is {MAX_EVAL_VALUE}.

The objective is to minimize the negative penalized specific energy absorption, defined as -1 * specific energy absorption if the intrusion length is 60 mm or less, and 100 * (intrusion length - 60) if it exceeds 60 mm. The structure is a star shaped crash-box with an initial height of 120 mm, clamped at the base and impacted by a 250 kg impactor from above at a velocity of 25.2 km/h. The design variables consist of 5 continuous variables: width (overall dimension along the x-axis, in mm) ranging over [60, 120], depth (overall dimension along the y-axis, in mm) ranging over [60, 120], notch_width (indentation length on each side of the cross-section along the x-axis, in mm) ranging over [0, 30], notch_depth (indentation length on each side of the cross-section along the y-axis, in mm) ranging over [0, 30], and thickness (uniform wall thickness at the notch midpoints, in mm) ranging over [0.7, 3.0]. Please note that while these specified ranges define the absolute implementational boundaries for each parameter, they serve primarily as a reference frame; you can flexibly control the actual search space depending on your optimization strategy. The evaluation budget is {MAX_EVAL_VALUE}.

search_space.reason: All variables are included since the evaluation budget is large enough to explore the whole search space.

algorithm.name: CMA-ES
algorithm.reason: The evaluation budget is moderate to explore the search space. The search space includes only continuous variables. CMA-ES can be a strong algorithm for continuous optimization problems and can effectively search the space and converge to good solutions within the given budget.

search_space.reason: The search space should be reduced its dimensionality due to the limited evaluation budget. The variables 'notch_width' and 'notch_depth' are fixed to 15, and 'thickness' is limited to the range [1.1, 2.6] to avoid impractical solutions.

algorithm.name: TPE
algorithm.reason: The search space has three continuous variables. TPE is suitable for finding a reasonable solution within a limited budget and can handle continuous optimization problems.
